disclaimer: The AML framework was overhauled by Federal Decree-Law 10 of 2025 (in force 14 October 2025) and Emiratisation targets carry monthly charges from 1 July 2026. UBO and PDPL are stable but enforcement guidance changes. Always check the regulator portal before filing.

esr.name: Economic Substance Regulations
esr.warning: Do NOT file ESR returns for current periods. The 9 Relevant Activities only matter for historical filings.

aml_cft.name: Anti-Money Laundering, Counter-Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation Financing

previous_law.status: Repealed and replaced by Federal Decree-Law 10 of 2025 with effect from 2025-10-14. Cited only for conduct predating that date.

key_changes_2025: Fines for legal persons raised to AED 5,000,000 to 100,000,000
Tax evasion added as a predicate offence
Virtual assets and VASPs explicitly covered
Proliferation financing added as a standalone offence category
aml_cft.dfsa_alignment: DFSA (DIFC) AML rulebook aligned with Federal Decree-Law 10 of 2025 effective 2026-03-02.

dnfbp_categories.notes: Must register on goAML, file Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs).

dnfbp_categories.category: Dealers in precious metals and stones
dnfbp_categories.notes: Cash transactions above AED 55,000 require reporting.
Must register on goAML and conduct EDD on clients.
Setup firms, PRO agencies, registered agents.
When acting on behalf of clients in financial transactions.

fines_aed.notes: Fine range for legal persons under Federal Decree-Law 10 of 2025 (previously AED 50,000 to 1,000,000 under FDL 20 of 2018). Administrative penalties for DNFBP registration or reporting breaches are set separately by the supervisory authorities.

aml_cft.vara_separate: Crypto / virtual asset businesses in Dubai fall under VARA Law 4 of 2022, V2.0 Rulebook effective 19 June 2025. Travel Rule applies. Monero and Zcash are banned. Federal Decree-Law 10 of 2025 now also covers virtual assets at the federal AML level.

emiratisation.name: Emiratisation (Nafis programme targets)
emiratisation.regulator: Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MOHRE)
emiratisation.applies_to: Private-sector companies registered with MOHRE (free zones are generally out of scope except where a zone opts in)

firms_50_plus.scope: Private-sector companies with 50 or more employees
firms_50_plus.target: Increase Emirati headcount in skilled roles by 1% every half-year (2% per year), toward a 10% Emiratisation rate by end of 2026 under the current programme.
firms_50_plus.h1_2026_deadline_status: PASSED. The 30 June 2026 deadline for the first-half 1% increment has expired.

non_compliance_charge.notes: From 1 July 2026 MOHRE collects AED 10,000 per month for each unachieved Emiratisation position (AED 120,000 per year per position). The rate started at AED 6,000/month in 2022 and rises AED 1,000 each year.

firms_20_to_49.scope: Private-sector companies with 20 to 49 employees in 14 selected economic sectors
firms_20_to_49.sectors_note: Selected sectors include information and communications, financial and insurance, real estate, professional and technical activities, administrative and support services, education, healthcare and social work, construction, wholesale and retail, transport and warehousing, hospitality, arts and entertainment, mining, and manufacturing.
firms_20_to_49.quota: At least 1 Emirati by end of 2024 and at least 2 Emiratis by end of 2025.

non_compliance_charge.notes: One-off yearly contributions: AED 96,000 collected in January 2025 for a 2024 shortfall and AED 108,000 collected in January 2026 for a 2025 shortfall (instalment options available). The regime remains operative for 2026 enforcement; no new quota beyond the 2-Emirati level has been announced as of 2026-07-02.

emiratisation.enforcement: MOHRE runs digital field monitoring to detect fake Emiratisation (ghost employees, paper-only contracts). When an Emirati employee leaves, the employer has two months to replace them before the position counts as unachieved.

ubo.name: Ultimate Beneficial Owner
ubo.applies_to: All UAE companies (mainland and most free zones)
ubo.threshold_notes: Direct or indirect ownership of 25% or more, or control by other means, triggers UBO disclosure.
ubo.filing_requirement: Maintain a UBO register internally and file with the licensing authority.
ubo.update_window_notes: Any change in UBO must be reported within 15 days.
exemptions: Companies wholly owned by federal or local UAE government
Companies in financial free zones (DIFC, ADGM) with separate UBO regimes

uae_federal.name: UAE Personal Data Protection Law
uae_federal.applies_to: Most UAE entities processing personal data, with some exemptions
uae_federal.exemptions: Personal data processed by individuals for personal use, security/intelligence agencies, judicial data, certain health data.

difc_dpl.name: DIFC Data Protection Law
difc_dpl.applies_to: Entities established in or operating from DIFC

adgm_dpr.name: ADGM Data Protection Regulations
adgm_dpr.applies_to: Entities established in or operating from ADGM
